assumption_label: floor $2M, IPO $500M, undisclosed 1x funding, operating 0x funding

hypotheses.name: Smart money
hypotheses.intuition: Top-40 investors by train-period success rate pick (or make) winners.
hypotheses.definition: Any of the 40 highest-success investors (>=10 train companies) is in the first round.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Big syndicate / consensus
hypotheses.intuition: More investors in the first round = more independent diligence agreeing.
hypotheses.definition: log(1 + distinct investors in first round), companies with >=1 recorded investor.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Champion rule (solo investor)
hypotheses.intuition: A single conviction investor beats committee consensus.
hypotheses.definition: Exactly one recorded first-round investor (vs 2+).

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Crowded category (Girard)
hypotheses.intuition: Mimetic competition in crowded categories kills outsized outcomes.
hypotheses.definition: log(1 + first equity rounds worldwide in same primary category, years t-1..t).

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Atypical combinations (Uzzi novelty)
hypotheses.intuition: Rare category pairings are novel ideas with fat right tails.
hypotheses.definition: -min over category pairs of log((obs+1)/(exp+1)), counts from earlier cohorts only; needs >=2 categories.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Kill zone
hypotheses.intuition: Big Tech having bought into a category chills independent big outcomes.
hypotheses.definition: A Big Tech acquirer bought a same-primary-category company in the 3 years before the first round.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: SF Bay Area
hypotheses.intuition: Density of talent, capital and acquirers.
hypotheses.definition: Crunchbase region == SF Bay Area.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Real-word name
hypotheses.intuition: Memorable dictionary names signal marketing sense.
hypotheses.definition: Lower-cased company name is a /usr/share/dict/words entry.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: .com domain
hypotheses.intuition: Owning the .com signals resources/seriousness.
hypotheses.definition: Homepage host ends in .com (NaN if no homepage recorded).

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Exact-match domain
hypotheses.intuition: Owning name.com exactly signals resources.
hypotheses.definition: Homepage host stem == normalised company name (NaN if no homepage).

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Form D timing
hypotheses.intuition: Late Form D filers are sloppy (or hiding); prompt filers are well-run.
hypotheses.definition: Original Form D filed >15 days after date of first sale (Rule 503 deadline); SEC DERA data sets matched by name+state. Exists only 2008+, so there is no train window.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Round-size surprise
hypotheses.intuition: A first round far above the category-year median means investors fought to get in.
hypotheses.definition: log(first round / median first round in same primary category and cohort year). Round size is NOT separately controlled here (it is the feature).

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Investor reputation momentum
hypotheses.intuition: Recent hit rate (3y) beats all-time reputation.
hypotheses.definition: Point-in-time max over first-round investors of exits realised in [d-3y,d) / portfolio before d; controls for all-time point-in-time exit rate.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Follow-the-follow-on
hypotheses.intuition: A seed investor re-upping in the next round has inside information.
hypotheses.definition: Any first-round investor also appears in the next equity round (Crunchbase has no lead flag, so participation not leadership). Defined only for companies that raised a next round with recorded investors - the tradable decision point is round 2.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Geographic arbitrage
hypotheses.intuition: The same signals are priced cheaper outside SF, so non-SF strong-signal deals return more.
hypotheses.definition: Among the top quintile of the train-fit prior composite P(big win), mean price-adjusted multiple of non-SF minus SF.

result.effect_units: multiple difference

hypotheses.name: Acquirer appetite - Big Tech
hypotheses.intuition: Categories Big Tech is actively buying produce exits.
hypotheses.definition: log(1 + Big Tech acquisitions in same primary category, prior 2 years).

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Acquirer appetite - PE / financial
hypotheses.intuition: Financial buyers provide a floor exit.
hypotheses.definition: log(1 + PE/financial-acquirer acquisitions in same category, prior 2 years).

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Acquirer appetite - strategic
hypotheses.intuition: Non-Big-Tech strategics buying in the category create exit liquidity.
hypotheses.definition: log(1 + other corporate acquisitions in same category, prior 2 years).

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Name semantics
hypotheses.intuition: Names far from their category's naming conventions stand out (or confuse).
hypotheses.definition: Cosine distance of name char-ngram TF-IDF from TRAIN centroid of its primary category (no taglines exist in this dataset).

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Company age at first round (nonlinear)
hypotheses.intuition: Too young = no traction, too old = stalled; a sweet spot exists.
hypotheses.definition: Years from founded_at to first round, 3-df natural spline, likelihood-ratio test.

result.effect_units: LR chi2

hypotheses.name: Syndicate diversity
hypotheses.intuition: Investors from many regions bring wider networks.
hypotheses.definition: Distinct investor home regions in the first round, controlling for syndicate size.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Contrarian but cheap (Thiel secret)
hypotheses.intuition: The contrarian portfolio fails on hit rate; a cheap entry price may rescue it.
hypotheses.definition: Below-train-median crowding AND above-train-median atypicality AND solo investor, restricted to the cheapest train-tercile entry price, vs all test deals.

result.effect_units: multiple difference

hypotheses.name: Accelerator-backed
hypotheses.intuition: YC/Techstars-style selection plus network.
hypotheses.definition: A named accelerator in the first round.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Angel-heavy syndicate
hypotheses.intuition: Rounds dominated by individuals lack institutional follow-on capacity.
hypotheses.definition: Share of first-round investors that are people (not organisations).

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Investor experience
hypotheses.intuition: Experienced investors select and help better.
hypotheses.definition: log(1 + mean prior Crunchbase deals of first-round investors, point-in-time).

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Local investors
hypotheses.intuition: Co-located investors monitor better, or local-only rounds lack reach.
hypotheses.definition: Share of first-round investors whose region equals the company's.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Category breadth
hypotheses.intuition: Listing many categories = unfocused.
hypotheses.definition: Number of Crunchbase categories listed.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: NY / Boston hub
hypotheses.intuition: Second-tier hubs also carry a density premium.
hypotheses.definition: Region is New York City or Boston.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Digit in name
hypotheses.intuition: Names with digits look amateurish.
hypotheses.definition: Normalised name contains a digit.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Short name
hypotheses.intuition: Short names are costlier to get, so signal resources.
hypotheses.definition: Length of normalised name.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Seed/angel entry beats Series A entry
hypotheses.intuition: Earlier entry is cheaper per unit of eventual outcome.
hypotheses.definition: Mean price-adjusted multiple of seed+angel first rounds minus Series A first rounds.

result.effect_units: multiple difference

hypotheses.name: Second-tier smart money
hypotheses.intuition: Investors ranked 41-120 carry signal without the top-40 price premium.
hypotheses.definition: A rank 41-120 investor (train success rate) in the first round and no top-40 investor.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Category momentum
hypotheses.intuition: Hot categories (deal count rising) get follow-on capital and exits.
hypotheses.definition: log((first rounds in category, year t + 1)/(year t-2 + 1)) within the US panel.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)

hypotheses.name: Speed to next round
hypotheses.intuition: Fast follow-on = traction. Tradable only at round 2.
hypotheses.definition: Years from first to next equity round, among companies that raised one.

result.effect_units: log-odds per SD (or per unit if binary)
